title: Phase I/II trial of gefitinib and RAD001 (everolimus) in patients (pts) with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)

sections.abstract: 7104 Background: The mechanisms of resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly understood but may be related, in part, to dysregulation of downstream apoptotic pathways, such as the PI3K/Akt/PTEN axis. In preclinical models, inhibition of the PI3K/Akt pathway restores gefitinib (Iressa™) sensitivity in resistant cell lines. mTOR is a serine/threonine kinase located downstream of Akt that regulates cellular growth and G1/S cell cycle progression. RAD001 is an orally available mTOR inhibitor that inhibits growth of cancer cell lines, including A549. We undertook this phase I/II study to characterize the safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), and antitumor activity of the combination of gefitinib and RAD001 in pts with advanced NSCLC with no prior history of EGFR-directed therapy. Methods: Phase I: 3-pt cohorts with no intrapatient escalation, at RAD001 dose levels of 5 and 10 mg daily. All pts received gefitinib 250 mg daily. PK studies were performed over a 3-week period during which pts received a single dose of RAD001 on day 1, followed by daily gefitinib on day 8, and then daily RAD001 on day 22. 6 pts will be treated at the MTD or highest RAD001 dose level prior to expanding to the phase II portion. Results: 6 pts have been enrolled to date. Patient characteristics: Female: 3; Karnofsky Performance Status median 80%; age median 62; prior chemotherapy median 2 (1–4). Toxicity (≥ Grade 2): by RAD001 dose level, 5 mg (n=3): 1 patient developed G2 stomatitis; 10 mg (n=3): 1 pt developed G2 diarrhea and G3 stomatitis, 1 pt developed G3 diarrhea, hypokalemia, and creatinine elevation, and G4 acidosis. Preliminary PK studies demonstrate AUC ratios (combination/alone) of 1.32 ± 0.46 for RAD001 and 1.15 ± 0.14 for gefitinib. Within the 5 mg dose level, a 25 pack-year smoking male pt with squamous cell carcinoma experienced a confirmed partial response; no EGFR exon 19 or 21 mutation was identified. Conclusions: 2 patients experienced dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) in the 10 mg dose level. 3 more patients will be enrolled in the RAD001 5 mg dose level prior to expanding to the phase II portion. Preliminary PK data suggests no significant interactions between the agents. Supported, in part, by Novartis.
